verdict.rationale: Flagsmith documents a self-hosted Edge Proxy that runs the Flagsmith Engine inside your own infrastructure, and server-side SDKs connect to it. That covers the relay part and keeps SDK traffic inside the network. The evidence never says flags keep being served when Flagsmith's hosted service is unreachable, and it only mentions server-side SDKs connecting. missing for 10: documented behavior during vendor outages (caching or offline serving), client-side SDK support via the proxy, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can run a relay/edge proxy so flags stay served when the vendor is unreachable and SDK traffic stays inside my network

citations.quote: The Flagsmith Edge Proxy is a service that you host yourself, that allows you to run an instance of the Flagsmith Engine close to your servers.
Run the Edge Proxy within in your own infrastructure and connect to it from your server-side SDKs
This means you can serve a very large number of requests close to your infrastructure and users, at very low latency.
